budgetBasis: No expansion family documents a recovery-time objective. eng/v1-production-slos.json sets 15-60 minute RTOs only for core-family production restores; every ceiling here is far tighter. All ceilings were fixed from the documented constants below before any failover run, and none was derived from or adjusted to an observed result.

Whole-recovery ceiling, fault to fully verified recovery: 180000 ms. This is the Jobs failover policy maximumRecoveryMilliseconds, which is the 180-second work deadline of the Jobs/Workflows physical promotion rehearsal (docs/jobs/failover.md) on the same digest-pinned PostgreSQL 18 image, the same synchronous remote_apply primary/standby pair and the same public provider multihost route (read-write target, one-second connect timeout).

Backend-termination and host-process-kill first-success ceiling: 45000 ms, the Jobs rehearsal's drain-phase observation deadline (docs/jobs/failover.md). Neither disturbance makes the database unavailable; recovery is one new connection (one-second connect timeout) plus, for leased products, expiry of the five-second lease the Jobs rehearsal uses.

Primary crash/restart and standby-promotion first-success ceiling: 60000 ms. Component sum fixed before running: 30 s server readiness (the runner's 150 x 200 ms startup deadline for a restart; pg_ctl promote -t 30 for a promotion) + 5 s standby reconnect retry (PostgreSQL's default wal_retrieve_retry_interval, needed before a remote_apply commit can succeed after a restart) + 10 s provider failed-host recheck interval (docs/jobs/failover.md) + 1 s connect timeout = 46 s, rounded up to the next whole minute.

A family-specific rehearsal that already carries a tighter deadline keeps it: the Projections physical promotion rehearsal has a 120-second work deadline (tests/BlueTusk.Projections.PhysicalRecoveryTests).

Projections.failoverSemantics: Projections receives source WAL at least once and applies it exactly once: derived documents, additive aggregates and the checkpoint commit in one transaction under a fenced database-clock lease, and the durable checkpoint deduplicates redelivery (docs/projections/RECOVERY.md). A physical promotion changes the source timeline, so recovery is an explicit operator rebuild of a new version rather than transparent resumption; that path is the dedicated promotion rehearsal.

scenarios.name: backend-termination
requiredChecks: interrupted worker stopped with a failure
interrupted apply rolled back whole, including its staged aggregate delta
replacement owner holds a newer fence
every tenant total and count equals the source exactly
every acknowledged source commit is present
every acknowledged source row is projected with its exact value
the interrupted source commit was applied after recovery

Documents.failoverSemantics: Documents promises durable acknowledged saves, all-or-nothing multi-document sessions, tenant isolation and revision compare-and-swap. A connection failure during commit can leave the outcome uncertain; the documented retry reads the document before re-inserting (docs/documents/README.md). Exactly-once applies to the database state of one save, not to a caller's retries.

no lost, duplicated or partial documents

Workflows.failoverSemantics: Workflows runs on Jobs leases: activities and compensations are at-least-once callbacks whose database effects are deduplicated, history replay must match persisted state, timers and signals survive, and a replaced owner's capability is fenced (docs/jobs/failover.md). The physical promotion step reuses the Jobs/Workflows rehearsal and judges its Workflows evidence; the fault step reuses the Workflows load harness's real process-death, lost-commit-acknowledgement and network-partition scenarios.
